q-5653.name: Question 1
q-5653.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the first term is $42$ and the common ratio is $-\frac{1}{5}?$
q-5653.worked_solution:
The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=42$ and $r=-\frac{1}{5}.$ Therefore, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{42[1-{(-\frac{1}{5})}^{N}]}{1-(-\frac{1}{5})} \\  & =\frac{42[1-{(-\frac{1}{5})}^{N}]}{\frac{6}{5}} \\  & =35[1-{(-\frac{1}{5})}^{N}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-5653.html:
Question 1
?

What is the sum of the first N terms of a geometric series if the first term is 42 and the common ratio is −15?

a
35[(15)N−1]
b
1052[(−15)N−1]
c
1052[(15)N+1]
d
35[1−(−15)N]
e
7−5N
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The sum of the first N terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r.

In this case, a1=42 and r=−15. Therefore, we have:

SN=42[1−(−15)N]1−(−15)=42[1−(−15)N]65=35[1−(−15)N]

q-39995.name: Question 2
q-39995.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $2+18+162+⋯?$
q-39995.worked_solution:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{18}{2} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case ${a}_{1}=2$ and $r=9.$ Substituting these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{2(1-{9}^{N})}{1-9} \\  & =\frac{2(1-{9}^{N})}{(-8)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(1-{9}^{N}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({9}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

q-39995.html:
Question 2
?

What is the sum of the first N terms of a geometric series 2+18+162+⋯?

a
 14(9N−1)
b
 9(2N−1)
c
 14(1−9N)
d
 9(1−2N)
e
 18(9N−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we determine the common ratio r for this geometric series:

r=a2a1=182=9

The sum of the first N terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r.

In this case a1=2 and r=9. Substituting these values into the formula for SN gives the following:

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r=2(1−9N)1−9=2(1−9N)(−8)=−14(1−9N)=14(9N−1)

q-67104.name: Question 3
q-67104.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $4$th term is $192$ and the common ratio is $4?$
q-67104.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 192 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {4}^{(4-1)} \\ 192 & =64{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=3$ and $r=4.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{3(1-{4}^{N})}{1-4} \\  & =\frac{3}{(-3)}(1-{4}^{N}) \\  & =-(1-{4}^{N}) \\  & ={4}^{N}-1\end{aligned}
$$

q-67104.html:
Question 3
?

What is the sum of the first N terms of a geometric series if the 4th term is 192 and the common ratio is 4?

a
4N−1
b
4(3N−1)
c
3N−1
d
4N−12
e
3(4N−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We use the formula for the nth term of a geometric sequence to determine a1:

an=a1rn−1192=a1⋅4(4−1)192=64a1a1=3

The sum of the first N terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

SN=a1(1−rN)1−r.

In this case, a1=3 and r=4. Substituting our values into the formula for SN gives:

SN=3(1−4N)1−4=3(−3)(1−4N)=−(1−4N)=4N−1
